about: Groupe SEB is the French small domestic appliances and cookware group behind Tefal, Krups, Rowenta, Moulinex, Seb, WMF, Lagostina and Supor. It sells kitchen, home-care and personal care products through retailers and professional coffee machines to commercial customers in 150 countries, with sales above 8 billion euros and about 33,000 employees. Founded in 1857, headquartered in Ecully near Lyon (Crunchbase shows Carros), listed on Euronext Paris (SK), with the Peugeot-family holding company FFP and Venelle controlling shares. Household brands with broad consumer recognition worldwide.

wiki.title: Groupe SEB
wiki.text: SEB S.A. or better known as Groupe SEB (Société d'Emboutissage de Bourgogne) is a large French consortium that produces small appliances, and it is the world's largest manufacturer of cookware. Notable brand names associated with Groupe SEB include All-Clad, IMUSA, Krups, Moulinex, Rowenta, Tefal (including OBH Nordica), Mirro and WMF Group. According to the Groupe SEB website, they have faced considerable competition from low-price Chinese competitors, but have managed to maintain a constant sales level. A large proportion of their product lines are now manufactured in China. Its headquarters are in Écully, a Lyon suburb.

about: Reddit is a San Francisco online platform of topic-based communities (subreddits) where users post, comment and vote, with hundreds of millions of monthly visitors. It earns revenue from advertising and from licensing its content for AI training, including deals with Google and OpenAI. Founded in 2005 and listed on the NYSE under RDDT since its March 2024 IPO. Very high consumer brand awareness among young, internet-native audiences, with growing brand marketing.

wiki.title: Reddit
wiki.what: American social news and discussion site
wiki.text: Reddit ( RED-it, stylized reddit) is an American social news website, news aggregator, forum and social media platform. Registered users (commonly referred to as "redditors") submit content to the site such as links, text posts, images, and videos, which are then voted up or down ("upvoted" or "downvoted") by other members. Posts are organized by subject into user-created boards called "subreddits". Submissions with more upvotes appear towards the top of their subreddit and, if they receive enough upvotes, ultimately on the site's front page. Reddit administrators moderate the communities. Moderation is also conducted by subreddit-specific mo

about: Central Retail is the largest retail group in Thailand, based in Bangkok, a subsidiary of Central Group, which runs department stores (Central, Robinson), supermarkets (Tops, Big C), fashion, specialty stores such as Power Buy and Supersports, and e-commerce, plus operations in Vietnam and Italy (Rinascente). Revenue is more than 200 billion baht. It is listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (CRC). Very high consumer visibility in Thailand and regional sports retail through Supersports.

Laopu Gold is a Beijing luxury gold jewellery brand known for jewellery made with traditional craftsmanship and a high-end store format in Chinese cities and selected overseas outlets. It listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (6181) in June 2025 and has grown rapidly, with a market value that moved sharply upward. Customers are affluent Chinese consumers who buy gold for gifts and investment. Funding of about CN¥225M was recorded in 2023. Strong luxury brand in China, with little international awareness.

US personal finance website and app that compares credit cards, mortgages, loans, savings accounts and insurance, offering advice and tools for consumers. Founded in 2009 in San Francisco and listed on Nasdaq (NRDS) since 2021, it earns commissions from financial institutions when users sign up for recommended products. It has tens of millions of monthly users and annual revenue of around 700 million dollars. Operations also in the UK and Canada, and it bought Ovid and others. Strong consumer brand awareness in the US and a prominent advertiser.

wiki.title: NerdWallet
wiki.text: NerdWallet is an American personal finance company, founded in 2009 by Tim Chen and Jacob Gibson. It has a website and app that earns money by promoting financial products to its users.

about: China's leading local services platform, running food delivery (Meituan Waimai and Keeta abroad), restaurant reviews, hotel and travel booking, instant retail, group buying and bike sharing. Earns commissions and advertising from merchants, with hundreds of millions of annual transacting users and revenue above 40 billion dollars. Headquartered in Beijing; founded 2010. Listed in Hong Kong (3690), with Tencent as a major shareholder. Everyday super-app for Chinese consumers, expanding into the Middle East and Brazil.

wiki.title: Meituan
wiki.text: Meituan (Chinese: 美团; pinyin: Měituán; formerly Meituan–Dianping) is a Chinese technology company that operates a platform for local services including on‑demand food delivery, in‑store services and consumer reviews under the Dazhong Dianping brand, hotel and travel bookings, and instant retail. The company is headquartered in Beijing and was founded in 2010 by Wang Xing. The company launched an initial public offering on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in September 2018. By the end of 2024, Meituan had over 770 million annual transacting users and over 14.5 million annual active merchants on its platform. Its international brand name used outsi

about: Italian world leader in hearing care retail, running about 10,000 shops under Amplifon, Miracle-Ear, NHS-affiliated and Elite Hearing brands in 26 countries, offering audiology services and hearing aids. Customers are people with hearing loss, mainly older consumers, with revenue near 2.3 billion euros. Headquartered in Milan; founded 1950. Listed on the Italian stock exchange (AMP). Known consumer brand in healthcare, and a sponsor of sports, such as AC Milan and Formula Racing.
cb_desc: Amplifon is a global leaderin the hearing care retail market,.

wiki.title: Amplifon
wiki.text: Amplifon SpA is an Italian company based in Milan and the world's largest hearing aid retailer.

about: Digital payments company running the PayPal wallet, Venmo, Braintree, Xoom and Honey and the PYUSD stablecoin, with over 430 million active accounts. Earns from transaction fees on merchants and consumers and credit products, with revenue near 32 billion dollars. Headquartered in San Jose, California; founded 1998, spun out of eBay in 2015. Listed on Nasdaq (PYPL). One of the best-known payment brands in the world, with sports sponsorship, including Formula 1 partnerships and stadium naming.

wiki.title: PayPal
wiki.text: PayPal Holdings, Inc. is an American multinational financial technology company operating an online payments system in the majority of countries that support online money transfers; it serves as an electronic alternative to traditional paper methods such as checks and money orders. The company operates as a payment processor for online vendors, auction sites and many other commercial and company users, which involve a fee. Established in March 2000 after a merger between Confinity and X.com, PayPal went public through an IPO in 2002. It became a wholly owned subsidiary of eBay later that year, valued at $1.5 billion. In 2015, eBay spun off Pa

about: Swedish fintech offering buy now pay later, pay in 30 days and instalment loans at checkout for millions of merchants, plus a shopping app, debit card and savings account. Customers are shoppers and retailers across Europe, the US and Australia, with more than 100 million users and revenue near 3 billion dollars. Headquartered in Stockholm; founded 2005. Listed on the New York Stock Exchange (KLAR) after a September 2025 IPO. Strong consumer brand and a Formula 1 sponsor (partner of Aston Martin) and other sports.

wiki.title: Klarna
wiki.text: Klarna Group plc is a Swedish financial technology company and digital bank. Founded in 2005 in Stockholm, Sweden, Klarna provides digital payments, short-term consumer credit, cards, banking services and merchant tools for online and in-store commerce. It is listed on the New York Stock Exchange and is best known for buy now, pay later payment products. Klarna Bank AB, the group's Swedish banking subsidiary, is authorized as a bank and supervised by the Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority. It provides financial services in the European Economic Area under European Union banking rules as well as areas outside the EEA, including in the Uni

about: FINN is a German car subscription provider where customers get a new or used car with insurance, registration and maintenance included for a monthly fee, fully online, with cars delivered to the door. Headquartered in Munich; founded 2019. Raised funding from investors such as BMW iVentures, with an operational scale in the tens of thousands of cars. Consumer-facing brand with growing awareness in Germany.

about: Kavak is a Mexican online used-car platform that buys, inspects, refurbishes and sells cars with financing and warranty, expanded to Brazil, Argentina, Chile, Colombia and the UAE. Headquartered in Mexico City; founded 2016. Became Latin America's first car unicorn, raising funding from SoftBank, General Atlantic and others, valued at 8.7 billion dollars in 2022. Private. Strong consumer brand in Mexico and active in football sponsorship.

wiki.title: Kavak (company)
wiki.text: Kavak is a Mexican company that operates a platform for buying, selling, financing, and managing new and used cars and commercial vehicles, for both individuals and businesses. It was founded in 2016 and is headquartered in Mexico City. Its founder and CEO is Carlos García Ottati.

about: Faire is a San Francisco online wholesale marketplace that connects independent retailers with small and mid-sized brands, offering ordering, payment terms and shipping. Retailers in North America, Europe and beyond buy gifts, home goods, apparel and food from hundreds of thousands of brands, and Faire earns commissions and fees. Founded in 2017, it has raised over $1.7bn and was valued at about $12.4bn in 2022. Private. B2B marketplace, well known among independent shop owners but not to the general public.

PetSmart is the largest US pet specialty retailer, based in Phoenix, Arizona, with about 1,650 stores in the US, Canada and Puerto Rico plus e-commerce. It sells pet food, supplies and accessories, and provides grooming, training, boarding (PetsHotel), in-store Banfield veterinary clinics and adoption events. Revenue is around $10bn. Owned by private equity firm BC Partners since 2015. Private, with funding mainly debt and equity from sponsors. Strong US consumer brand with mass-market advertising.

wiki.title: PetSmart
wiki.text: PetSmart is an American chain of pet superstores, which sell pet products, services, and small pets. As of 2020, PetSmart has more than 1,650 stores in the United States and Canada. PetSmart stores sell pet food, pet supplies, pet accessories, and small pets. Stores also provide services including grooming, dog daycare, dog and cat boarding, veterinary care via in-store third-party clinics, and dog training. They also offer dog and cat adoption via in-store adoption centers facilitated by the non-profit PetSmart Charities. Founded in 1986 by Jim and Janice Dougherty, the company opened its first two stores in 1987 in Phoenix, Arizona, under t

about: Carro is a Singapore-headquartered online used car marketplace and automotive platform operating in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong and Taiwan, combining car sales, financing, insurance, subscriptions and an auction business. Founded in 2012, it became a unicorn in 2021 and has raised over $1.1bn including debt, with backers like SoftBank and Temasek. Private. Strong consumer brand in Singapore and nearby markets, with significant marketing spend.

wiki.title: Carro
wiki.text: Carro (Ligurian: O Caro, locally U Caru) is a comune (municipality) at the Province of La Spezia in the Italian region Liguria, located about 60 kilometres (37 mi) southeast of Genoa and about 25 kilometres (16 mi) northwest of La Spezia. Carro borders the following municipalities: Carrodano, Castiglione Chiavarese, Deiva Marina, Maissana, Sesta Godano, Varese Ligure.

about: QVC is a Rocky Mount, North Carolina (corporate base West Chester, Pennsylvania) video and online retailer, selling home, fashion, beauty, jewellery and electronics through TV shopping channels and digital platforms in the US, UK, Germany, Japan and Italy. It is a subsidiary of Qurate Retail, and its sister brand HSN is also part of the group. Revenue runs near $10bn. Qurate is listed on Nasdaq (QRTEA). Well-known consumer shopping brand with an older, primarily female audience.

wiki.title: QVC
wiki.text: QVC (short for "Quality, Value, Convenience") is an American free-to-air television network and a flagship shopping channel specializing in televised home shopping, owned by QVC Group (formerly Qurate Retail Group). Founded in 1986 by Joseph Segel in West Chester, Pennsylvania, United States, QVC broadcasts to more than 350 million households in seven countries, including channels in the UK, Germany, Japan, and Italy, along with a joint venture in China with China National Radio called CNR Mall. In 2024, the total revenue for the year was $10 billion. As of December 2013, Halo2Cloud holds the network's record for most units sold in a day of 3

about: Ocado Group is a British online grocery technology company, based in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, which developed a robotic warehouse and fulfilment system licensed to grocers such as Kroger, Coles, Aeon and Sobeys, and runs the Ocado Retail UK online supermarket with Marks and Spencer. Revenue from technology fees and retail is over GBP 3bn. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (OCDO). Ocado is a well-known UK consumer brand, though its technology business is B2B.

wiki.title: Ocado
wiki.text: Ocado Group plc ( ok-AH-doh) is a British business based in Hatfield, England, which licenses grocery technology. It also owns a 50% share in the UK grocery retail business Ocado Retail Ltd (the other 50% is owned by UK retailer Marks & Spencer). The company is listed on the London Stock Exchange and is a constituent of the FTSE 250 Index.

about: Diebold Nixdorf is a North Canton, Ohio supplier of ATMs, self-checkout, point-of-sale systems and related software and services to banks and retailers worldwide, with roughly 20,000 employees and revenue near $3.7bn. It restructured through a Chapter 11 filing in 2023 and emerged with debt reduced, relisting on the NYSE (DBD). B2B equipment brand, the ATMs are widely seen though consumers seldom know the brand.

wiki.title: Diebold Nixdorf
wiki.what: American multinational financial and retail technology company
wiki.text: Diebold Nixdorf, Incorporated is an American multinational financial and retail technology company based in North Canton, Ohio. It specializes in the sale, manufacture, installation, and service of self-service transaction systems (such as ATMs and currency processing systems), point-of-sale terminals, physical security products, and software and related services for global financial, retail, and commercial markets. Diebold Nixdorf has a presence in around 130 countries, and the company employs approximately 23,000 people. Founded in 1859 in Cincinnati, Ohio as the Diebold Bahmann Safe Company, the company eventually changed its name to Diebo

about: Vinted is a Lithuanian online marketplace for second-hand fashion, based in Vilnius, where individuals buy and sell clothes, shoes and accessories, with buyers paying a protection fee. It has over 100 million registered members in about 20 markets across Europe and the US, and reported revenue of around EUR 800m. Valued at EUR 5bn in a 2024 secondary sale. Private, backed by Insight and Accel. Strong consumer brand across Europe, with large advertising spending.

wiki.title: Vinted
wiki.text: Vinted Group UAB (formerly Mano Drabužiai, meaning "my clothing") is a Lithuanian technology company best known for its online marketplace Vinted. Vinted is the leading second-hand fashion marketplace in Europe. According to the company, its mission is to 'make second-hand first choice worldwide'. The company operates the Vinted Marketplace (its peer-to-peer resale platform), Vinted Go (logistics and shipping services), Vinted Pay (in-app payment solutions), and Vinted Ventures (an investment arm supporting the circular economy). Headquartered in Vilnius, Lithuania, it also has offices in Germany and the Netherlands and employs more than 2,20

about: FEMSA is a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational and one of Latin America's largest beverage and retail groups. It owns about 47 percent of Coca-Cola FEMSA, the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler, and operates OXXO, a chain of over 22,000 convenience stores, as well as pharmacy and fuel retail, and has held a stake in Heineken. Listed on the Mexican exchange and the NYSE (FMX). OXXO is a household brand across Latin America.

wiki.title: FEMSA
wiki.text: Fomento Económico Mexicano, S.A.B. de C.V., doing business as FEMSA, is a Mexican multinational beverage and retail company headquartered in Monterrey, Mexico. It operates the largest independent Coca-Cola bottling group in the world and the largest convenience store chain in Mexico. FEMSA reported revenues of US$26.9 billion for 2019, making it the fifth largest company of Mexico. It has operations in Latin America mainly through bottling plants, convenience stores, drugstores, fuel stations, and third-party logistic services, and in the United States, where it participates in the jan-san distribution industry. It is well known in Mexico for

about: Autodoc is a Berlin-based online retailer of vehicle spare parts and accessories, founded in 2008 by Alexej Erdle, selling over a million parts to drivers and garages in more than 25 European countries via its own web shops. Revenue is over a billion euros. Reported funding of about 580 million euros; an IPO was planned but postponed in 2023. Consumer e-commerce brand with high awareness in Germany and Eastern Europe, with football and motorsport sponsorship.

wiki.title: Autodoc
wiki.text: AUTODOC SE is an e-commerce company selling auto parts and related products in 27 European countries. Its main customers are individuals and smaller workshops. The company sells via its online shops, mobile app, AUTODOC MARKETPLACE, and third-party marketplaces.

about: Seven & i Holdings is a Tokyo-based Japanese retail holding company, owner of 7-Eleven convenience stores (including 7-Eleven Inc. in North America with about 85,000 stores worldwide), Ito-Yokado supermarkets and Denny's Japan, listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (3382). Founder-family and shareholders resisted Couche-Tard's takeover proposal in 2024-25, which was withdrawn. Revenue is over 11 trillion yen. Customers are consumers, with very high brand awareness globally.

wiki.title: Seven & I Holdings
wiki.text: Seven & I Holdings Co., Ltd. (株式会社セブン&アイ・ホールディングス) is a Japanese diversified retail holdings company headquartered in Nibanchō, Chiyoda, Tokyo. On September 1, 2005, it was established as a result of the integration of three companies: Ito-Yokado, Seven-Eleven Japan, and Denny's Japan. The purpose of this establishment was to create a holding company that would own these three companies. The background behind this decision was that the parent company, Ito-Yokado, was facing deteriorating performance, while its subsidiary, Seven-Eleven Japan, was experiencing growth in both sales and profits and was performing well. Following a downturn in the

about: FlixBus is a European intercity bus brand headquartered in Munich that works on a network model: partner coach companies run buses under the green FlixBus branding while Flix handles routes, ticketing and marketing. It carries tens of millions of passengers across Europe and the US, since buying Greyhound in 2021, and also runs FlixTrain. Founded 2013. Parent Flix SE is owned by General Atlantic, Permira, Silver Lake and the founders. Strong consumer brand across Europe.

wiki.title: FlixBus
wiki.text: FlixBus (German pronunciation: ['flɪksbʊs]; styled FLiXBUS) is a German brand that offers intercity bus services in 45 countries in Europe, North America, South America, Asia and Oceania, with over 300,000 daily connections. It is owned by Flix SE, which also operates FlixTrain, Kâmil Koç and Greyhound Lines. FlixBus operates buses or – in many cases – just handles network planning, scheduling, pricing, booking and marketing, as well as customer service, for a commission. In April 2022, the company converted from a GmbH structure to an SE structure and was renamed Flix SE. By 2026, Flix was serving more than 8,700 destinations with 4,700 buse

about: Carsome is a Malaysian online used-car marketplace headquartered in Petaling Jaya that lets consumers buy and sell inspected, certified cars with financing and insurance, and also provides B2B dealer auctions across Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Singapore. Founded 2015, it raised more than 400 million dollars from Temasek, Gaw Capital and others, achieving unicorn status in 2021. Customers are consumers and dealers. Strong consumer brand in Malaysia.

wiki.title: Carsome
wiki.what: Malaysian online used car trading platform
wiki.text: Carsome Group (Carsome) is a Malaysian online used car trading platform that operates in Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, and Singapore. It was founded in 2015 with the aim of digitize the traditional used car buying and selling process by leveraging technology and providing a convenient and transparent experience for both buyers and sellers. It is recognized as Malaysia's first technology unicorn after announcing the closure of its US$170 million (RM705.5 million) of funding in September 2021.

about: Paris-based online marketplace for pre-owned luxury fashion, founded 2009, with more than 30 million members worldwide. Valued at about $1.7 billion in 2022. Consumer brand with strong awareness among fashion buyers. Operates in about 40 countries, earning commission on sales and verifying authenticity of items. Strong brand among fashion resale buyers. The company was founded in 2009 and is based in Paris and has offices in New York and London.

wiki.title: Vestiaire Collective
wiki.what: Online retailer of used luxury goods
wiki.text: Vestiaire Collective is a global platform for buying and selling pre-owned luxury and designer fashion. The platform connects buyers and sellers of secondhand luxury and designer items, with listings digitally verified and curated by an internal team supported by AI. Buyers can choose physical authentication through international hubs or opt for direct shipping. In 2020, Vestiaire Collective was recognized as the 11th French Unicorn part of the French Tech Next 40/120 list.

about: Plano, Texas-based beauty retail and distribution company, founded 1964, with about 5,000 stores selling Sally Beauty and CosmoProf hair and nail products. Listed on the NYSE (SBH). Known US consumer retailer. Customers are professional stylists and consumers, with stores in the US and Europe. Moderate consumer awareness. Sally Beauty has about 30,000 employees and operates the Sally Beauty Supply and Beauty Systems Group chains selling to professional salons and individual shoppers.

wiki.title: Sally Beauty Holdings
wiki.text: Sally Beauty Holdings, Inc. is an American international specialty retailer and distributor of professional beauty supplies with revenues of more than $3.9 billion annually. Through the Sally Beauty Supply and Beauty Systems Group businesses, the Company sells and distributes through over 4,000 stores, including approximately 200 franchised units, throughout the United States, the United Kingdom (Sally Beauty UK), Belgium (pro- duo 40SHOPS M&A ), Canada, Chile, Peru, Puerto Rico, Mexico (2000 Amstrong McCall 130 shops M&A), France, Ireland, Germany and The Netherlands. Sally Beauty Supply stores offer more than 6,000 products for hair, skin,

about: Cencosud is a Chilean multinational retailer, based in Santiago, operating supermarkets (Jumbo, Santa Isabel, Disco, Wong), the Paris department stores, Easy home improvement, shopping centres (Costanera Center) and financial services across Chile, Argentina, Brazil, Peru and Colombia, plus the US via The Fresh Market. Listed on the Santiago Stock Exchange (CENCOSUD), with revenue of over 15 billion dollars. Very strong consumer brands across Latin America.

wiki.title: Cencosud
wiki.text: Cencosud S.A. is a publicly traded retail company based in Chile. It is the largest retail company in Chile and the third largest listed retail company in Latin America, competing with the Brazilian Companhia Brasileira de Distribuição and the Mexican Walmart de México y Centroamérica as one of the largest retail companies in the region. The company has more than 1045 stores in Latin America.

about: QVC Group (formerly Qurate Retail) is a US video and online commerce group, headquartered in West Chester, Pennsylvania, operating the QVC and HSN television shopping networks, Zulily and Cornerstone brands such as Ballard Designs and Frontgate. It sells home, fashion, beauty and jewellery to consumers through TV, web and apps. Listed on Nasdaq (QVCGA). Revenue has declined to around 10 billion dollars. Well known in the US among home shoppers.

wiki.title: QVC Group
wiki.text: QVC Group (formerly Qurate Retail, Inc., also known as Qurate Retail Group), is an American media conglomerate controlled by company chairman John C. Malone, who owns a majority of the voting shares.

about: PDD Holdings is the parent of Pinduoduo, the Chinese social e-commerce marketplace, and Temu, its international shopping platform launched in 2022 which sells low-priced goods across the US, Europe and other markets. It earns from advertising, merchant fees and transaction services, with revenue above $50 billion. Originally based in Shanghai, it re-domiciled to Ireland in Dublin and is listed on Nasdaq (PDD). Temu is a heavy advertiser, including a major Super Bowl presence, so it has strong consumer visibility.

wiki.title: Pinduoduo
wiki.text: Pinduoduo (Chinese: 拼多多; pinyin: Pīnduōduō) is a Chinese online retailer, with a focus on the traditional agriculture industry. The business is the largest asset of PDD Holdings, a company domiciled in the Cayman Islands and headquartered in Ireland that also owns the online marketplace Temu.

about: eBay is a San Jose, California online marketplace, founded in 1995 and listed on Nasdaq (EBAY), where consumers and businesses buy and sell new and used goods, from cars parts to collectibles, via auctions and fixed-price listings. It earns fees and advertising, with about $10 billion in revenue and over 130 million active buyers. Operating in dozens of countries, it is a globally recognised consumer brand and has previously sponsored sport.

wiki.title: EBay
wiki.text: eBay Inc. ( EE-bay, styled as ebay) is an American multinational e-commerce company based in San Jose, California, that allows users to buy or view items via retail sales through online marketplaces and websites in 190 markets worldwide. Sales occur either via online auctions or "Buy It Now" instant sales, and the company charges commissions to sellers upon sale. eBay was founded by Pierre Omidyar in September 1995. In 2021, eBay had approximately 17 million global sellers; in 2023, it reported 132 million annual active buyers worldwide and handled $73 billion in transactions, 48% of which were in the United States. In 2023, the company had a

about: French consumer electronics and appliance retailer formed by the 2016 merger of Fnac and Darty, headquartered in Ivry-sur-Seine. Sells electronics, books, music, appliances and tickets through stores, franchises and online in France, Belgium, Spain, Portugal and Switzerland; revenue around EUR 8 billion. Listed on Euronext Paris (FNAC). Mass-market consumer brand in France.

wiki.title: Fnac Darty
wiki.text: Fnac Darty SA, formerly Groupe Fnac S.A., is a multinational retail company headquartered in Ivry-sur-Seine, France. It took its current name after acquiring Darty plc (formerly Kesa Electricals plc and Darty Limited) in 2016.

about: Swedish fast-fashion group founded 1947 with brands H&M, COS, Weekday, Monki, & Other Stories and Arket. Sells through about 4,000 stores in 79 markets and online; revenue about SEK 235 billion. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (HM B). Family-controlled by Persson. One of the best-known fashion brands in the world.

wiki.title: H&M
wiki.text: H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB, commonly known by its brand name H&M, is a Swedish multinational clothing company headquartered in Stockholm. Built on a fast fashion business model, the retailer sells apparel, accessories, and homeware. The company operates thousands of stores across 75 geographical markets and employs over 171,000 people worldwide. H&M is the second-largest international clothing retailer after Inditex. H&M was founded by Erling Persson in 1947 under the name Hennes. The CEO of H&M from 2020 to 2024 was Helena Helmersson. The current CEO, as of January 2024, is Daniel Ervér.

about: Canadian e-commerce platform serving millions of merchants, and the leading commerce software for online stores. Ottawa-based, listed on TSX and Nasdaq (SHOP). Revenue about USD 9 billion. Shopify was founded in 2006 by Tobi Lutke and sells Shopify Plus to large merchants, with Shop Pay as its checkout wallet. It is a regular name in Formula 1 paddock partnerships. Known in business and tech, and has held Formula 1 team sponsorship deals.

wiki.title: Shopify
wiki.text: Shopify Inc. is a Canadian multinational e-commerce company headquartered in Ottawa, Ontario, that operates a cloud e-commerce management platform (CEMP) for retail point-of-sale systems. The company has over five million customers and processed US$292.3 billion in transactions in 2024, of which 57% was in the United States. Major customers include Tesla, LVMH, Nestlé, PepsiCo, AB InBev, Kraft Heinz, Lindt, Whole Foods Market, Red Bull, and Hyatt. The company's software has been praised for its ease of use and reasonable fee structure. It has been described as the "go-to e-commerce platform for startups".

about: Signet Jewelers is the world's largest diamond jewellery retailer, listed on the NYSE (SIG), with US roots in Akron, Ohio and a legal base in Bermuda. It operates about 2,600 stores under Kay Jewelers, Zales, Jared, Piercing Pagoda, Banter and the online retailer Blue Nile, with revenue of about $6-7 billion. Customers are consumers buying engagement rings, wedding and gift jewellery. Highly recognised in US consumer advertising.

wiki.title: Signet Jewelers
wiki.text: Signet Jewelers Ltd. (Ratner Group 1949–1993 then Signet Group plc to September 2008) is, as of 2025, the world's largest retailer of diamond jewellery. The company is domiciled in Bermuda and headquartered in Akron, Ohio through the Fairlawn suburb, and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange. The group operates in the middle-market jewellery segment and holds number one positions in the US, Canada, and UK speciality jewellery markets. Certain brands, like Ernest Jones in the UK, operate in the upper middle market. Signet Jewelers owns and operates the companies Blue Nile, Zales, Kay Jewelers, Jared, JamesAllen.com, and others.

about: Zalando is a Berlin based European online fashion and lifestyle platform, selling clothing, shoes and beauty from thousands of brands to about 50 million active customers in around 25 countries. Founded in 2008 and listed on the Frankfurt exchange (ZAL), it has revenue of over 10 billion euros and acquired About You in 2025. Very strong consumer brand awareness in Germany and across Europe, with sports and entertainment partnerships.

wiki.title: Zalando
wiki.what: Multinational e-commerce company specializing in shoes and fashion
wiki.text: Zalando SE is a German multinational e-commerce company headquartered in Berlin, specializing in fashion, beauty, and footwear. It is Europe's largest online fashion retailer. Founded in 2008 by Robert Gentz and David Schneider, the company has expanded its operations to 30 European markets, currently serving a customer base of 62 million active users. Beyond its primary multi-brand online shopping platform, which includes its own private label brands, Zalando operates the shopping club Lounge by Zalando, maintains physical outlet stores in Germany, and provides logistics and marketing services for retail partners. In November 2025, Zalando f

about: American Eagle Outfitters is a Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania multi-brand specialty apparel retailer selling jeans, tops and accessories under American Eagle, Aerie intimates and the Todd Snyder menswear brand. Customers are young consumers shopping through about 1,100 stores and online across the US, Canada, Mexico and licensed international markets. Revenue is around 5 billion dollars. Founded in 1977, it is listed on the NYSE (AEO). Strong consumer brand, particularly among teens and college students in North America.

wiki.title: American Eagle Outfitters
wiki.text: American Eagle Outfitters, Inc. is an American clothing and accessories retailer headquartered at SouthSide Works in the South Side Flats neighborhood of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. It was founded in 1977 by brothers Jerry and Mark Silverman as a subsidiary of Retail Ventures, Inc., a company that also owned and operated Silverman's Menswear. The Silvermans sold half their ownership interests in 1980 to the Schottenstein family and the remainder in 1991. about: Copart is a US online vehicle auction company, headquartered in Dallas, Texas. It runs auctions of salvage and clean-title cars, trucks and motorcycles through websites and about 200 physical yards in the US, Canada, UK, Germany, Spain, Brazil, UAE and other countries. Sellers are insurers, dealers, fleets and charities, and buyers include rebuilders, dealers and export buyers; Copart earns seller and buyer fees. Annual revenue is several billion dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (CPRT). B2B-oriented brand with limited general consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Copart
wiki.text: Copart, Inc. is a multinational provider of online vehicle auction and remarketing services to automotive resellers such as insurance, rental car, fleet, and finance companies in 11 countries: the US, Canada, the UK, Germany, Ireland, Brazil, Spain, UAE, Bahrain, Oman, and Finland. Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Copart has more than 200 physical locations, where it houses more than 10,000 acres of vehicle inventory. Copart sells used, wholesale and repairable vehicles in weekly and bi-weekly online auctions to buyers ranging from consumers to automotive businesses. Copart provides vehicle sellers with a range of services to process and sell

about: Global-e is a cross-border e-commerce platform, founded in 2013 and operating mainly out of Israel, that lets merchants sell to shoppers abroad by handling local pricing, duties and taxes, payments, shipping and returns. Customers are big fashion, beauty and lifestyle brands such as those on Shopify, with Shopify as a key partner and shareholder. It listed on Nasdaq as GLBE in 2021 after funding rounds, with Crunchbase showing about 100 million dollars from 2020. B2B and mostly invisible to shoppers, so low brand awareness.

Africa's largest food retailer, operating supermarkets and hypermarkets under Shoprite, Checkers, Checkers Hyper, Usave and OK Furniture banners, plus liquor, pharmacy and convenience formats. It sells groceries, fresh food and household goods mainly to mass-market and middle-income shoppers in South Africa and, historically, other African countries, and also runs the Xtra Savings loyalty programme and money-transfer services. Headquartered in Brackenfell near Cape Town, it is listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (SHP) and has well over 2,800 outlets and around 150,000 staff. Very high consumer brand visibility across Southern Africa.

wiki.title: Shoprite Holdings
wiki.text: Shoprite (officially Shoprite Holdings Ltd) is Africa's largest supermarket retailer, and one of the largest retail companies in the world. The company's headquarters are in Cape Town, South Africa, where it was founded in 1979. Shoprite is a public company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and A2X Markets in South Africa, with secondary listings on both the Namibian and Lusaka stock exchanges. about: Global diversified healthcare company, listed on the NYSE (ABT), selling medical devices (FreeStyle Libre glucose monitors, heart devices), diagnostics, nutrition (Similac, Ensure) and established pharmaceuticals in over 160 countries. Revenue about 42 billion dollars, around 114,000 employees, founded in 1888 and based in Abbott Park, Illinois. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and consumers. Well-known consumer health brand worldwide.

wiki.title: Abbott Laboratories
wiki.what: American global medical devices and health care products company
wiki.text: Abbott Laboratories, commonly known as Abbott, is an American multinational medical devices and health care company founded in Chicago with headquarters in Abbott Park, Illinois. The company produces pharmaceuticals for sale outside the United States (13% of 2024 revenues), diagnostic products (20% of 2024 revenues), nutritional products (22% of 2024 revenues), and medical devices (45% of 2024 revenues). Abbott operates in over 160 countries and sources from at least 62 suppliers worldwide. Abbott's products include Pedialyte, Similac, BinaxNOW, Ensure, Glucerna, ZonePerfect, FreeStyle Libre, i-STAT and MitraClip. The company is ranked 107th

about: Anglo-Swedish pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Cambridge, UK, listed in London, Stockholm and on the NYSE (AZN). Develops oncology, cardiovascular, respiratory and rare-disease medicines, including Tagrisso, Farxiga and Imfinzi, and vaccines. Sells to health systems worldwide, with revenue about 54 billion dollars and roughly 90,000 employees. B2B pharma brand, but visible through sports sponsorship history and brand marketing.

wiki.title: AstraZeneca
wiki.text: AstraZeneca plc () (AZ) is a Swedish–British multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company with its headquarters at the Cambridge Biomedical Campus in Cambridge, England. It has a portfolio of products for major diseases in areas including oncology, cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, infection, neuroscience, respiratory, and inflammation. The company was founded in 1999 through the merger of the Swedish Astra AB and the British Zeneca Group (itself formed by the demerger of the pharmaceutical operations of Imperial Chemical Industries in 1993). Zeneca shareholders received 53.5% of the shares, while Astra shareholders received the rem

about: German life science company based in Leverkusen, listed in Frankfurt, with pharmaceuticals (Xarelto, Eylea), crop science (Monsanto acquisition in 2018) and consumer health (Aspirin, Bepanthen). Founded in 1863, around 95,000 employees and revenue about 46 billion euros. Customers are farmers, patients, pharmacies and consumers. Very strong consumer and corporate brand; long-time sports sponsor, including Bayer 04 Leverkusen.

wiki.title: Bayer
wiki.what: German multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company
wiki.text: Bayer AG (English: , commonly pronounced ; German: [ˈbaɪɐ] ) is a German multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company and is one of the largest pharmaceutical companies and biomedical companies in the world. Headquartered in Leverkusen, Bayer's areas of business include pharmaceuticals, consumer healthcare products, agricultural chemicals, seeds and biotechnology products. The company is a component of the EURO STOXX 50 stock market index. Bayer was founded in 1863 in Barmen as a partnership between dye salesman Friedrich Bayer (1825–1880) and dyer Johann Friedrich Weskott (1821–1876). The company was established as a dyestuffs prod

about: Biopharmaceutical company headquartered in New York, listed on the NYSE (BMY), developing medicines in oncology (Opdivo), immunology and cardiovascular (Eliquis), hematology and neuroscience, including after acquiring Celgene in 2019. Sells to hospitals and pharmacies. Revenue about 46 billion dollars with 34,000 employees. Well-known pharma brand to healthcare professionals, less so to consumers.

wiki.title: Bristol Myers Squibb
wiki.text: Bristol-Myers Squibb Company, doing business as Bristol Myers Squibb, is an American multinational pharmaceutical company headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey. The company's primary products are apixaban (Eliquis) for people with atrial fibrillation (30% of 2025 revenues); nivolumab (Opdivo), used to treat certain types of cancer (21% of 2025 revenues); lenalidomide (Revlimid), used to treat multiple myeloma, smoldering myeloma, and myelodysplastic syndromes (6% of 2025 revenues); abatacept (Orencia), used to treat autoimmune diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis (8% of 2025 revenues); pomalidomide (Pomalyst/Imnovid), an anti-cancer medicat

about: French global pharmaceutical group in Paris, listed on Euronext (SAN) and NASDAQ, with immunology (Dupixent), vaccines (flu and others), rare diseases and consumer healthcare (Opella, partially sold in 2025). Revenue about 43 billion euros, around 82,000 employees. Customers include hospitals, governments and pharmacies. Well known to healthcare professionals, and a visible brand in Europe.

wiki.title: Sanofi
wiki.what: French multinational pharmaceutical and healthcare company
wiki.text: Sanofi S.A. is a French multinational pharmaceutical and healthcare company headquartered in Paris. The corporation was established in 1973 and merged with Synthélabo in 1999 to form Sanofi-Synthélabo. In 2004, Sanofi-Synthélabo merged with Aventis and renamed to Sanofi-Aventis, which were each the product of several previous mergers. It changed its name back to Sanofi in May 2011. The company trades as "SAN" on Euronext Paris and "SNY" on Nasdaq in the United States, and is a component of the Euro Stoxx 50 stock market index. In 2023, the company was ranked 89th in the Forbes Global 2000. Sanofi engages in the research and development, manuf

about: Waltham, Massachusetts-based life sciences company, listed on the NYSE (TMO), supplying lab instruments, reagents, consumables, diagnostics and clinical research services to pharma, biotech, hospitals and academic labs. Brands include Fisher Scientific, Applied Biosystems and Invitrogen. Revenue about 43 billion dollars with around 125,000 employees. B2B scientific brand, famous within labs, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Thermo Fisher Scientific
wiki.what: Provisioner of scientific consumables, equipment, and services
wiki.text: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. is an American life science and clinical research company. It is a global supplier of analytical instruments, clinical development solutions, specialty diagnostics, laboratory, pharmaceutical and biotechnology services. Based in Waltham, Massachusetts, Thermo Fisher was formed through the merger of Thermo Electron and Fisher Scientific in 2006. Thermo Fisher Scientific has acquired other reagent, consumable, instrumentation, and service providers, including Life Technologies Corporation (2013), Alfa Aesar (2015), Affymetrix (2016), FEI Company (2016), BD Advanced Bioprocessing (2018), and PPD (2021). It ranked 10

about: Washington DC-headquartered science and technology conglomerate, listed on the NYSE (DHR), owning life sciences brands (Beckman Coulter, Cytiva, Leica, Pall, SCIEX, Abcam, Aldevron), and diagnostics (Cepheid). Founded in 1984 by the Rales brothers, it spun off Fortive in 2016, Envista in 2019 and Veralto in 2023. Revenue about 24 billion dollars, around 63,000 employees. B2B brand known in labs and industry.

wiki.title: Danaher
wiki.text: Danaher is a surname. Notable people with the surname include: Declan Danaher (born 1980), English Rugby union player Jody Danaher, Irish rugby player John Danaher (ethicist) Irish legal scholar and philosopher specialized in the legal and ethical impacts of AI and emerging technologies John Danaher (martial artist) (born 1967), New Zealand Brazilian jiu-jitsu and mixed martial arts instructor John Danaher (VC) (1860–1919), Irish recipient of the Victoria Cross John A. about: Foster City, California biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (GILD), a leader in HIV (Biktarvy), hepatitis C and B, oncology (Trodelvy, Yescarta from Kite) and COVID antiviral Veklury. Revenue about 29 billion dollars with 17,000+ employees. Founded in 1987. Strong in HIV prevention marketing, a B2B pharma brand with some consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Gilead Sciences
wiki.text: Gilead Sciences, Inc. () is an American biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Foster City, California, that focuses on researching and developing antiviral drugs used in the treatment of HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B, hepatitis C, influenza, and COVID-19. It also develops medicines in therapeutic areas such as oncology and inflammation and cell therapy. In 1987, Michael L. Riordan founded the company under the name Oligogen. The original name was a reference to oligonucleotides, small strands of DNA used to target genetic sequences. Gilead held its initial public offering in 1992, and successfully developed drugs including Tamiflu and Vistide th

about: British pharmaceutical and vaccines group in London, listed on the LSE and NYSE (GSK), with vaccines (Shingrix, Arexvy), HIV medicines (ViiV Healthcare) and specialty medicines. Consumer healthcare split out as Haleon in 2022. Revenue about 31 billion pounds with about 70,000 employees. Founded in 1715 via predecessors. Strong brand in healthcare, with sports sponsorship history.

wiki.title: GSK plc
wiki.text: GSK plc (an abbreviation of its former name GlaxoSmithKline plc) is a British multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company. It was established in 2000 by a merger of Glaxo Wellcome and SmithKline Beecham, which was itself a merger of a number of pharmaceutical companies around the Smith, Kline & French firm. It is headquartered in London, England. GSK is the tenth-largest pharmaceutical company in the world by earnings, $9.32 billion in 2025 with $42.4 billion in revenues in the same period. As of February 2026 it is the 175th most valuable company in the world and the 12th most valuable pharmaceutical company with a market capitali

about: Durham, North Carolina-based provider of clinical research, healthcare data and analytics to pharma companies, listed on the NYSE (IQV), formed by merger of Quintiles and IMS Health in 2016. Pharma, biotech and medical device clients outsource trials to it and buy prescription and market data from it. Revenue about 15 billion dollars with around 88,000 employees. B2B healthcare data brand.

wiki.title: IQVIA
wiki.text: IQVIA Holdings, Inc. is an American health information technology and clinical research company headquartered in Durham, North Carolina. The company provides clinical research services, healthcare analytics, technology solutions, and commercial outsourcing services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and healthcare organizations worldwide. IQVIA operates through three business segments: Technology & Analytics Solutions, Research & Development Solutions, and Contract Sales & Medical Solutions. Through its technology and analytics business, the company maintains access to more than one billion supposedly anonymized patient records

about: Swiss pharmaceutical group in Basel, listed on SIX (NOVN) and NYSE (NVS), focused on innovative medicines after spinning off Sandoz in 2023 and previously the Alcon eye care business. Products include Entresto, Cosentyx, Kisqali and Leqvio. Revenue about 50 billion dollars with around 76,000 employees. Strong corporate brand, an active sponsor of sports and culture.

wiki.title: Novartis
wiki.text: Novartis AG is a Swiss multinational pharmaceutical corporation based in Basel, Switzerland. Novartis is one of the largest pharmaceutical companies in the world and was the eighth largest by revenue in 2024. Novartis manufactures the drugs clozapine (Clozaril), diclofenac (Voltaren; sold to GlaxoSmithKline in 2015 deal), carbamazepine (Tegretol), valsartan (Diovan), imatinib mesylate (Gleevec/Glivec), cyclosporine (Neoral/Sandimmune), letrozole (Femara), methylphenidate (Ritalin; produced by Sandoz since 2023), terbinafine (Lamisil), deferasirox (Exjade), and others. Novartis was formed in 1996 by the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz. It was

about: Basel-based generic and biosimilar medicines company, spun off from Novartis in 2023 and listed on SIX Swiss Exchange (SDZ). Sells off-patent medicines in over 100 countries to hospitals and pharmacies. Revenue about 10 billion dollars with around 23,000 employees. Well-known pharma brand, active in sports sponsorship.

Pfizer is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, headquartered in New York, and best known for the Comirnaty Covid-19 vaccine (with BioNTech), Prevnar, Eliquis, Ibrance and Lipitor heritage. It sells prescription medicines and vaccines to health systems and governments worldwide, with revenue of roughly $60 billion and about 80,000 staff. Founded in 1849, listed on the NYSE (PFE). Very high consumer awareness, with a history of sports partnerships in some markets.

wiki.title: Pfizer
wiki.what: American multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology corporation
wiki.text: Pfizer Inc. ( FY-zər) is an American multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology corporation headquartered at The Spiral in Manhattan, New York City. Founded in 1849 in New York by German entrepreneurs Charles Pfizer and Charles F. Erhart, Pfizer is one of the oldest pharmaceutical companies in North America. Pfizer develops and produces medication and vaccines for immunology, oncology, cardiology, endocrinology, and neurology. about: Zoetis is the world's largest animal health company, headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey and spun out of Pfizer in 2013. It sells medicines, vaccines, diagnostics and genetic tests for pets and livestock, including Simparica Trio, Apoquel and Cytopoint, in more than 100 countries, with revenue of about $9 billion. Listed on the NYSE (ZTS). Vets and pet owners know its products, though the corporate brand is B2B.

wiki.title: Zoetis
wiki.text: Zoetis Inc. (), headquartered in Parsippany, New Jersey, is the largest producer of medicine and vaccinations for pets and livestock worldwide. The company's products include antiparasitics, vaccines, products that relieve itch, anti-infectives, products that alleviate pain, animal health diagnostics, as well as hormones, cardiopulmonary, topical and oral hygiene therapeutics, central nervous system drugs, diuretics, antiemetic, euthanasia, and hepato-digestive products. about: Eli Lilly is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, headquartered in Indianapolis and founded in 1876. It develops and sells prescription medicines including the GLP-1 drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, Verzenio, Taltz, Jardiance with Boehringer Ingelheim, Humalog insulin and others, to health systems, pharmacies and patients in over 100 countries. Revenue exceeded $45 billion in 2024 and market capitalisation passed $700 billion in 2025. Listed on the NYSE under LLY. Major global corporate brand, though consumer promotion is limited by regulation.

wiki.title: Eli Lilly
wiki.what: American pharmacist, Union Army officer, businessman, philanthropist (1838–1898)
wiki.text: Eli Lilly (July 8, 1838 – June 6, 1898) was an American Union Army officer, pharmacist, chemist, and businessman who founded Eli Lilly and Company. Lilly enlisted in the Union Army during the American Civil War and recruited a company of men to serve with him in the 18th Independent Battery Indiana Light Artillery. He was later promoted to major and then colonel, and was given command of the 9th Indiana Infantry Regiment. Lilly was captured in September 1864 and held as a prisoner of war until January 1865. After the war, he attempted to run a plantation in Mississippi, but it failed and he returned to his pharmacy profession after the death

wiki.title: Eli Lilly and Company
wiki.text: Eli Lilly and Company, doing business as Lilly, is an American multinational pharmaceutical company headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, with offices in 36 countries. Its products are marketed in approximately 90 countries. The company was founded in 1876 by Eli Lilly, a pharmaceutical chemist and Union army veteran during the American Civil War for whom the company was later named. The company is ranked 4th on the list of largest biomedical companies by revenue and is the most valuable pharmaceutical company worldwide. about: Braskem is Latin America's largest petrochemical company and a leading producer of biopolymers, headquartered in Sao Paulo. It makes polyethylene, polypropylene, PVC and green polyethylene from sugarcane ethanol, with plants in Brazil, the US, Mexico and Germany, and sells resins to plastics converters in packaging, automotive and construction. Revenue is around $15-20 billion. Controlled by Novonor (formerly Odebrecht) and Petrobras, and listed on B3 (BRKM5) and the NYSE (BAK). Pure B2B brand, though Braskem has appeared in Brazilian sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: Braskem
wiki.text: Braskem S.A is a Brazilian petrochemical company headquartered in São Paulo. The company is the largest petrochemical company in Latin America and has become a major player in the international petrochemical market (8th largest resin producer worldwide).

about: Suzano is a Brazilian pulp and paper company headquartered in Sao Paulo, the world's largest producer of market eucalyptus pulp after its 2019 merger with Fibria. It also sells paper, packaging board and consumer tissue under brands such as Report and Neve, and moved into the international tissue business with Kimberly-Clark in 2025. Customers are tissue, paper and packaging manufacturers worldwide, mainly in China, Europe and North America. Controlled by the Feffer family and listed on B3 (SUZB3) and NYSE (SUZ). Largely B2B, with some Brazilian consumer brands.

wiki.title: Suzano
wiki.text: Suzano is a municipality in São Paulo state, Brazil. It is part of the Metropolitan Region of São Paulo. The population is 300,559 (2020 est.) in an area of 206.24 km2 (79.63 sq mi). The elevation is 749 m. Suzano's industrial growth was boosted in the past by the availability of available sites for companies to set up and by its access to highways that lead to the interior and coast of the state. The Índio Tibiriçá, Rodoanel and Henrique Eroles highways pass directly through Suzano. Suzano has direct access to the Ayrton Senna Highway, the Anchieta Highway and indirect access to Mogi-Dutra and consequently to Dutra itself.

about: Takeda is Japan's largest pharmaceutical company, headquartered in Tokyo and founded in 1781. It sells prescription medicines in gastroenterology (Entyvio), rare diseases, plasma-derived therapies, oncology and neuroscience (Vyvanse), after acquiring Shire in 2019, with operations in around 80 countries and revenue of more than 4 trillion yen. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems. Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (4502) and the NYSE (TAK). Well-known corporate brand but little consumer advertising.

wiki.title: Takeda
wiki.text: Takeda (武田, Takeda, "warrior rice paddy") or Takeda (竹田, Takeda, "bamboo rice paddy") is a Japanese family name. Throughout the course of the Sengoku period (16th century) of Japan, the famed Takeda clan of Kai Province had many descendant branch families. about: COFCO is China's largest state-owned food and agriculture group, headquartered in Beijing, with grain trading and processing, oilseeds, sugar, meat, dairy, wine, and food brands, along with real estate and financial arms. COFCO International is a major global agricultural trader. It owns or sells consumer brands such as Fortune cooking oil, Great Wall wine, Lohas and Mengniu stakes. It is on the Fortune Global 500, with hundreds of billions of yuan in revenue. Crunchbase shows about 11 billion dollars of funding. Strong consumer brand recognition in China.

wiki.title: COFCO Group
wiki.what: Chinese state-owned food processing holding company
wiki.text: China Oil and Foodstuffs Corporation (Chinese: 中国粮油食品（集团）有限公司), commonly known as COFCO (Chinese: 中粮), is a Chinese state-owned food processing holding company. COFCO Group is China's largest food processor, manufacturer and trader. It is also one of Asia's leading agribusiness groups alongside Wilmar International. Its headquarters are in the COFCO Fortune Plaza (中粮福临门大厦) in Chaoyang District, Beijing.

about: UPM-Kymmene is a Finnish forest industry group, headquartered in Helsinki, that produces pulp, paper, specialty labels (UPM Raflatac), plywood and timber, and renewable fuels and biochemicals from wood. Customers are packaging, printing, construction and fuel industries globally. It is a major forest owner, employs around 17,000 people and has revenue of about 10 billion euros. Listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (UPM). Crunchbase shows about 1.85 billion in funding. B2B industrial brand with strong recognition in Finland, though little among consumers elsewhere.

wiki.title: UPM (company)
wiki.text: UPM-Kymmene Oyj is a Finnish forest industry company. UPM-Kymmene was formed by the merger of Kymmene Corporation with Repola Oy and its subsidiary United Paper Mills Ltd in 1996. UPM consists of six business areas: UPM Fibres, UPM Energy, UPM Raflatac, UPM Specialty Papers, UPM Communication Papers and UPM Plywood. The Group employs around 17,000 people and it has production plants in 11 countries. UPM shares are listed on the NASDAQ OMX Helsinki stock exchange. about: Fresenius Medical Care is a German healthcare group, based in Bad Homburg, and the world's largest provider of kidney dialysis, running roughly 3,900 dialysis clinics and treating around 290,000 patients, and manufacturing dialysis machines, dialysers and related products. Revenue is close to 20 billion euros and it has about 120,000 employees. It is listed on the Frankfurt exchange as FME and was majority-owned by Fresenius SE until a 2023 restructuring. B2B and patient-facing healthcare, with a corporate rather than consumer brand.

wiki.title: Fresenius Medical Care
wiki.what: German medical supply and dialysis company
wiki.text: Fresenius Medical Care AG & Co. KGaA is a German healthcare company which provides kidney dialysis services through a network of 4,171 outpatient dialysis centers, serving 345,425 patients. The company primarily treats end-stage renal disease (ESRD), which requires patients to undergo dialysis 3 times per week for the rest of their lives. With a global headquarters in Bad Homburg vor der Höhe, Germany, and a North American headquarters in Waltham, Massachusetts, it has a 38% market share of the dialysis market in the United States. about: Amgen is a US biotechnology company headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California, listed on Nasdaq (AMGN), founded in 1980. It sells biologic medicines including Enbrel, Prolia and Xgeva, Repatha, Otezla, Aranesp and Tezspire, plus biosimilars, and bought Horizon Therapeutics in 2023 for about $28 billion. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and health systems worldwide. Revenue is around $33 billion with roughly 28,000 employees. It is a very large pharma brand, known to doctors and investors more than the general public.

wiki.title: Amgen
wiki.text: Amgen Inc. is an American multinational biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Thousand Oaks, California. The company is ranked 18th on the list of largest biomedical companies by revenue. The name "AMGen" is a portmanteau of the company's original name, Applied Molecular Genetics. The company's major products are Prolia and XGEVA (denosumab) to treat osteoporosis and bone diseases ($6.6 billion in total 2025 revenues), Repatha (evolocumab) to treat hyperlipidemia ($3.0 billion in 2025 revenues), Otezla (apremilast) to treat psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis ($2.3 billion in 2025 revenues), Enbrel (etanercept) to treat autoimmune diseases

about: Alltech is a private animal health and nutrition company based in Nicholasville, Kentucky, founded in 1980 by Dr Pearse Lyons. It makes feed supplements, yeast products and mineral nutrition for livestock and pets, with operations in over 100 countries, and runs the Lexington Brewing and Distilling Company producing Kentucky Ale and Town Branch bourbon. Revenue is about 2 billion dollars. It was title sponsor of the FEI World Equestrian Games in 2010 and 2018. B2B brand with some consumer-facing drinks and equestrian profile.

wiki.title: Alltech
wiki.text: Alltech is an American company, headquartered in Nicholasville, Kentucky, with operations in animal feed, meat, brewing, and distilling. Alltech develops agricultural products for use in both livestock and crop farming, as well as products for the food industry. Alltech operates under three main divisions: animal nutrition and health; crop science; and, food and beverage.

about: GlaxoSmithKline, now GSK plc, is a London-headquartered global pharmaceutical and vaccines company, with medicines for respiratory disease, HIV (ViiV), oncology and vaccines such as Shingrix and Arexvy. Its consumer health division was demerged as Haleon in 2022. It is listed on the London and New York exchanges (GSK) with revenue of about 30 billion pounds. It sells to health systems and doctors, and its brand is globally known, with sport sponsorship history.

wiki.title: GSK plc
wiki.text: GSK plc (an abbreviation of its former name GlaxoSmithKline plc) is a British multinational pharmaceutical and biotechnology company. It is headquartered in London, England. GSK is the tenth-largest pharmaceutical company in the world by earnings, $9.32 billion in 2025 with $42.4 billion in revenues in the same period. about: Swiss healthcare group in Basel and one of the world's biggest drug and diagnostics companies, with its Genentech unit in the US and Chugai in Japan. Key medicines include Ocrevus, Hemlibra, Tecentriq, Herceptin and Avastin, while its diagnostics unit sells lab analyzers, glucose monitors and tests. Customers are hospitals, labs, health systems and payers, and sales are over 60 billion Swiss francs. Employs roughly 100,000 people and is a recognised corporate name, though sold to professionals rather than consumers.

wiki.title: Roche
wiki.text: F. Hoffmann-La Roche AG, commonly known as Roche (), is a Swiss multinational holding healthcare company that operates worldwide under two divisions: Pharmaceuticals and Diagnostics. Its holding company, Roche Holding AG, has shares listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange. The company headquarters are located in Basel. Roche is the fifth-largest pharmaceutical company in the world by revenue and the leading provider of cancer treatments globally. In 2023, the company’s seat in the Forbes Global 2000 was 76. about: US biotechnology company in Cambridge, Massachusetts, focused on neurology and neuroscience. Its products include multiple sclerosis drugs such as Tecfidera, Vumerity and Tysabri, the spinal muscular atrophy treatment Spinraza, and Leqembi for Alzheimer's disease, developed with Eisai. Customers are hospitals, neurologists and payers worldwide, and it also earns royalties from partner products. Founded in 1978 and listed on Nasdaq (BIIB). Strong healthcare brand among doctors and patients.

wiki.title: Biogen
wiki.text: Biogen Inc. is an American multinational biotechnology company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States specializing in the treatment of neurological diseases. about: Pharmaceutical services company, once the largest contract research organisation in the world, running clinical trials for drug makers and providing commercial consulting. Went public on the NYSE in 2013 after private equity ownership by TPG and Bain, then merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form QuintilesIMS, renamed IQVIA in 2017. The Quintiles name no longer exists as a separate company. B2B pharma services brand.
