wiki.title: IQVIA
wiki.text: IQVIA Holdings, Inc. is an American health information technology and clinical research company headquartered in Durham, North Carolina. The company provides clinical research services, healthcare analytics, technology solutions, and commercial outsourcing services to pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, and healthcare organizations worldwide. IQVIA operates through three business segments: Technology & Analytics Solutions, Research & Development Solutions, and Contract Sales & Medical Solutions. Through its technology and analytics business, the company maintains access to more than one billion supposedly anonymized patient records

about: US life sciences and diagnostics tools company, spun out of Hewlett-Packard in 1999 and listed on the NYSE (A). Sells liquid and gas chromatography, mass spectrometers, genomic and cell analysis instruments, software and services to pharmaceutical, chemical, food and environmental laboratories worldwide. Revenue is around 6 to 7 billion USD, with roughly 18,000 employees, and a large share comes from consumables and services. B2B brand with strong visibility in laboratories and among scientists.

wiki.title: Agilent Technologies
wiki.text: Agilent Technologies, Inc. is an American global company headquartered in Santa Clara, California, that provides instruments, software, services, and consumables for laboratories. Agilent was established in 1999 as a spin-off from Hewlett-Packard. The resulting initial public offering of Agilent stock was the largest in the history of Silicon Valley at the time. From 1999 to 2014, the company produced optics (LED, laser), semiconductors, EDA software and test and measurement equipment for electronics; that division was spun off to form Keysight. Since then, the company has continued to expand into pharmaceutical, diagnostics & clinical, and a

about: Belgian global biopharmaceutical company, listed on Euronext Brussels (UCB), focused on neurology and immunology with drugs such as Keppra and Briviact for epilepsy, Cimzia for autoimmune diseases and Bimzelx for psoriasis. Founded in 1928, with around 9,000 employees and revenue of several billion euros, controlled by the Janssen family. Customers are patients through hospitals and pharmacies worldwide. Strong healthcare brand among doctors, with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: UCB (company)
wiki.text: UCB (Union Chimique Belge) is a multinational biopharmaceutical company headquartered in Brussels, Belgium. UCB is an international company with revenue of €4.178 billion in 2016 which focuses primarily on research and development, specifically involving medications centered on epilepsy, Parkinson's disease, and Crohn's disease. The company's efforts are focused on treatments for severe diseases treated by specialists, particularly in the fields of central nervous system (CNS) disorders (including epilepsy), inflammatory disorders (including allergy), and oncology. Every three years, the company presents the UCB Award under the patronage of t

about: Henry Schein is a Melville, New York distributor of health care products and services, listed on Nasdaq as HSIC, supplying dental practices, physician offices, laboratories and animal health clinics. It sells consumables, equipment, software and practice management services in more than 30 countries, with about 25,000 team members and revenue of around $12 billion. Customers are dentists, doctors and vets. The business was founded in 1932. Well known among dental and medical professionals, but not a consumer brand.

wiki.title: Henry Schein
wiki.text: Henry Schein, Inc. is an American distributor of health care products and services, with operations in 33 countries and territories. It is the world's largest provider of health care solutions to office-based dental and medical practitioners.

about: Zimmer Biomet is a Warsaw, Indiana-based orthopaedic medical device maker, listed on the NYSE (ZBH), selling knee, hip, and shoulder implants, surgical tools and robotics such as ROSA. Revenue is about $7.5 billion. Customers are hospitals and surgeons. Warsaw, Indiana is the 'orthopaedic capital of the world'. B2B brand with moderate consumer awareness through patient advertising.

wiki.title: Zimmer Biomet
wiki.text: Zimmer Biomet Holdings, Inc. is a publicly traded American medical device company. It was founded in 1927 to produce aluminum splints. The firm is headquartered in Warsaw, Indiana, where it is part of the medical devices business cluster. In 2001, Zimmer was spun off from Bristol Myers Squibb and began trading on the New York Stock Exchange, on August 7, under the ticker symbol “ZMH”. In November 2011, the company acquired ExtraOrtho, Inc. (ExtraOrtho). In January 2012, the company acquired Reno, Nevada-based Synvasive Technology, Inc. On June 29, 2015, the company changed the ticker symbol to "ZBH" to reflect its acquisition of Biomet. On Ja

about: ASSA ABLOY is a Swedish world leader in door opening solutions, making locks, access control, security doors, biometric readers, digital keys and entrance automation under brands like Yale, HID, Chubb, Mul-T-Lock and Assa. Customers are builders, property owners, governments and consumers, with revenue exceeding 150 billion Swedish kronor and about 60,000 employees in more than 70 countries. Headquartered in Stockholm and listed on Nasdaq Stockholm. Yale is a recognised consumer brand, while the group name is mostly B2B.

wiki.title: Assa Abloy
wiki.text: Assa Abloy AB is a Swedish company that sells products and services related to locks, doors, gates, and entrance automation, as well as controlling access and confirming identities with keys, cards, tags, mobile, and biometric identity verification systems. The company was formed in 1994, when Assa AB was separated from Swedish security firm Securitas AB. Shortly thereafter, Assa AB merged with the Finnish high security lock manufacturer Abloy Oy (based in Joensuu, a then subsidiary of the Finnish company Wärtsilä). The company was introduced to the Stockholm Stock Exchange later the same year. Assa Abloy has since made over 300 acquisitions

about: Japan's long-established technology group, a supplier of IT services, network equipment, satellite systems, biometrics (including face recognition) and defence electronics. Customers are governments, telecom carriers, utilities and enterprises worldwide. NEC is more than a century old, employs over a hundred thousand people and is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. Known for NEC brand PCs historically and for global sports and event sponsorship, so it has decent consumer recognition in Japan and some markets worldwide.

wiki.title: NEC
wiki.text: NEC Corporation (日本電気株式会社, Nippon Denki Kabushiki gaisha; an acronym for Nippon Electric Company) is a Japanese multinational conglomerate corporation headquartered at the NEC Supertower in Minato, Tokyo, Japan. It sells IT and network services, including cloud computing, artificial intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT) platform, and telecommunications equipment and software to business enterprises, communications services providers and to government agencies. It is one of the five largest defense contractors in Japan. NEC was one of the world's largest personal computer and semiconductor manufacturers from the 1980s to the 2000s, but h

about: The Clorox Company is a US consumer products maker founded in 1913 and based in Oakland, California, with brands including Clorox bleach and disinfecting wipes, Brita, Glad, Kingsford, Hidden Valley, Burt's Bees and Pine-Sol. Customers are retailers such as Walmart and Costco, with sales of about $7 billion a year and roughly 8,000 staff. Listed on the NYSE (CLX). Very high consumer brand visibility in North America.

wiki.title: Clorox
wiki.what: American global manufacturer and marketer based in Oakland, California
wiki.text: The Clorox Company (formerly Clorox Chemical Company) is an American multinational manufacturer and marketer of consumer and professional products. Clorox ranked annually on the Fortune 500 list from 2000 to 2024, where it last held the #485 spot. Clorox products are sold primarily through mass merchandisers, retail outlets, e-commerce channels, distributors, and medical supply providers. Clorox brands include its namesake bleach and cleaning products as well as Burt's Bees, Formula 409, Glad, Hidden Valley, Kingsford, Kitchen Bouquet, KC Masterpiece, Liquid-Plumr, Brita (in the Americas), Mistolin, Pine-Sol, Poett, Green Works Cleaning Produ

about: Alcon is a Swiss-American eye care company, headquartered in Vernier near Geneva, that makes surgical devices and intraocular lenses plus contact lenses and eye drops under brands such as Dailies, Air Optix, Systane and Clareon. Customers are surgeons, optometrists and consumers, with sales of about $10 billion in 140 countries. Spun out from Novartis in 2019 and listed on the SIX and NYSE (ALC). Well-known eye care brand.

wiki.title: Alcon
wiki.what: Swiss-American pharmaceutical and medical device company
wiki.text: Alcon Inc. (German: Alcon AG) is a Swiss-American pharmaceutical and medical device company specializing in eye care products. Alcon is incorporated in the Canton of Fribourg, Switzerland, and its global headquarters are located in Geneva, but its main operational base is in Fort Worth, Texas, United States, where it employs about 4,500 people. Alcon was a subsidiary of Novartis until April 2019, when it was spun out into a separate publicly traded company. Alcon itself has a number of subsidiaries, including Aerie Pharmaceuticals, focused on therapies for glaucoma and other diseases of the eye, and WaveLight, which develops and manufactures

about: Boston Scientific is a Marlborough, Massachusetts medical device maker with products in cardiology, urology, endoscopy, neuromodulation and peripheral interventions, such as stents, catheters, pacemaker leads and the Watchman device. Customers are hospitals and clinicians in about 100 countries; revenue is around 16 billion dollars with some 48,000 employees. Founded in 1979, it trades on NYSE (BSX). Known to clinicians but with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Boston Scientific
wiki.text: Boston Scientific Corporation (BSC) is an American biotechnology and biomedical engineering firm and multinational manufacturer of medical devices used in interventional medical specialties, including interventional radiology, interventional cardiology, peripheral interventions, neuromodulation, neurovascular intervention, electrophysiology, cardiac surgery, vascular surgery, endoscopy, oncology, urology and gynecology. The company is known for developing the Taxus Stent, a drug-eluting stent that is used to open clogged arteries. BSC is headquartered in Marlborough, Massachusetts and incorporated in Delaware.

about: Bausch + Lomb is a Bridgewater, New Jersey eye health company making contact lenses (Biotrue, Ultra, PureVision), lens care solutions, eye drops (Lumify), surgical equipment and prescription ophthalmic products, with revenue near 4.5 billion dollars and sales in over 100 countries. Customers are consumers, eye doctors and hospitals. It was spun off in an IPO from Bausch Health in 2022 and trades on NYSE and TSX (BLCO). A strong consumer healthcare brand worldwide.

wiki.title: Bausch & Lomb
wiki.text: Bausch & Lomb (stylized as Bausch + Lomb since 2010) is an eye health products company based in Vaughan, Ontario. It produces contacts and intraocular lenses, medications, and eye surgery-related products. Founded 1853 in Rochester, New York by optician John Bausch and financed by Henry Lomb, it was one of the oldest continually operating companies in the United States, which was publicly traded on New York Stock Exchange before being acquired by the private equity firm Warburg Pincus in 2007. The company was then sold to the Canadian company Bausch Health in 2013. As of 2022, the company employs about 12,900 people.

about: Linde is the world's largest industrial gases company, listed on Nasdaq and NYSE (LIN), formed in 2018 from the merger of Linde AG and Praxair. It supplies oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen, argon and specialty gases, plus engineering and equipment, to healthcare, chemicals, energy, food, electronics and manufacturing customers in over 100 countries. Revenue is about $33 billion and it has around 65,000 employees. The Crunchbase listing shows the Woking, UK base of its engineering operations. B2B giant with low consumer awareness.

BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company) is a Franklin Lakes, New Jersey medical technology company, making syringes, needles, catheters, infusion pumps, diagnostics and biosciences products. Founded in 1897, it has about 70,000 employees and revenue of around $20 billion, listed on the NYSE (BDX). It sells to hospitals, labs and pharma companies worldwide. A B2B healthcare brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: BD (company)
wiki.text: Becton, Dickinson and Company (BD; also Becton Dickinson or Becton) is an American multinational medical technology company that manufactures and sells medical devices, instrument systems, and reagents. BD also provides consulting and analytics services in certain areas. BD is ranked #211 in the 2024 Fortune 500 list based on its revenues for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023.

about: Fresenius is a German health care group headquartered in Bad Homburg, with business units Fresenius Kabi (injectable drugs, clinical nutrition, biosimilars), Fresenius Helios (Europe's largest private hospital operator) and a stake in dialysis company Fresenius Medical Care, formerly a subsidiary. Revenue is about 22 billion euros with roughly 190,000 employees. Founded in 1912 and listed on the Frankfurt exchange (FRE). Mainly B2B with a strong Helios brand in Germany and Spain.

wiki.title: Fresenius
wiki.text: Fresenius is a German surname. Notable people with the surname include: Carl Remigius Fresenius (1818–1897), German chemist Christian Fresenius (1749-1811), German Jurist and writer Eduard Fresenius ( (1874–1946), German businessman, founder of Fresenius Georg Fresenius (1808–1866), German botanist Wilhelm Fresenius (1913–2004), German chemist from Mainz

wiki.title: Fresenius (company)
wiki.text: Fresenius SE & Co. KGaA is a German multinational health care company based in Bad Homburg vor der Höhe. It provides products and services for dialysis in hospitals, as well as inpatient and outpatient medical care. The company is involved in hospital management and in engineering and services for medical centers and other health care facilities. The company was ranked 411th in the 2023 Forbes Global 2000 list.

about: Hims & Hers Health is a telehealth company, listed on the NYSE (HIMS) and based in San Francisco, selling consumer health products by online consultation and subscription. Its range covers erectile dysfunction, hair loss, skin care, mental health, weight loss and women's health. Founded in 2017 as Hims, it earns revenue of over $1.5 billion with millions of subscribers. Strong US direct-to-consumer brand awareness, with heavy advertising, including a Super Bowl presence.

wiki.title: Hims & Hers Health
wiki.text: Hims & Hers Health, Inc., doing business as hims, is an American telehealth company headquartered in San Francisco. It provides prescription medications, over-the-counter medications, and personal care products through a direct-to-consumer subscription model.

about: Solventum is a health care company spun off from 3M in April 2024, based near Minneapolis, Minnesota (Maplewood) and listed on the NYSE (SOLV). It sells medical and surgical products, wound care, dental solutions, purification and filtration, and health information software, with annual revenue near US$8 billion, to hospitals, clinicians and dentists worldwide. Funding of about $648M was recorded in 2025. Customers are health providers. The brand is new, but products such as Tegaderm and Filtrete heritage are familiar to professionals.

wiki.title: Solventum
wiki.text: Solventum Corporation is an American health care company that was spun off from 3M on April 1, 2024.

about: Flo Health is a London-based digital health company, founded in 2015 by Dmitry and Yury Gurski, that operates the Flo app for period tracking, fertility, pregnancy and women's health, using artificial intelligence to provide cycle predictions and health insights. It has hundreds of millions of downloads and tens of millions of monthly active users globally, and earns from premium subscriptions. General Atlantic led a 200 million dollar investment in 2024, valuing it at about 1 billion dollars. A high-profile consumer health brand, particularly with young women.

Global maker of sleep apnea and respiratory care devices: CPAP machines, masks and the myAir app, plus digital health software, sold to patients through home-medical-equipment dealers and online. Revenue is around 5 billion dollars with about 10,000 staff, in 140 countries. Listed on NYSE (RMD) and ASX. Consumer-facing health brand with strong awareness among sleep apnea patients. It was founded in 1989 in Australia by Peter Farrell and now has its operating base in San Diego.

wiki.title: ResMed
wiki.text: Resmed Inc. is a medical equipment company based in San Diego, California, and founded in Australia. It primarily provides cloud-connectable medical devices for the treatment of sleep apnea (such as CPAP devices and masks), chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and other respiratory conditions. Resmed produced hundreds of thousands of ventilators and bilevel devices to help treat the respiratory symptoms of patients with COVID-19. Resmed also provides software to out-of-hospital care agencies to streamline transitions of care into and between these care settings for seniors and their care providers (i.e. home health, hospice, skilled

about: Danish hearing healthcare group behind Oticon, Bernafon and Philips-licensed hearing aids, Interacoustics diagnostics and Audika retail clinics, selling to audiologists and retail clinics in over 130 countries. Revenue is above 20 billion Danish kroner. Listed on Nasdaq Copenhagen. Strong brands among audiologists and a visible consumer presence through retail clinics. Demant is controlled by the William Demant Foundation, which gives it a long-term family-style ownership structure.

wiki.title: Demant
wiki.text: Demant A/S is a Danish international company involved with hearing care, hearing aids and audiometric equipment. It is headquartered in Smørum (northwest of Copenhagen) and had a revenue of kr. 22,400,000,000 in 2024.

about: Saskatoon-based crop nutrient company listed on the NYSE and TSX (NTR), the world's largest provider of potash, nitrogen and phosphate fertilizers and operating a large retail network (Nutrien Ag Solutions). Revenue about 25 billion dollars. Customers are farmers and retailers. B2B brand, though visible in agriculture.

wiki.title: Nutrien
wiki.text: Nutrien is a Canadian fertilizer company based in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan. It is the largest producer of potash, second largest producer of nitrogen fertilizer in the world and generally the 2nd largest in fertilizers worldwide. It has over 2,000 retail locations across North America, South America, and Australia with more than 23,500 employees. It is listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (symbol NTR) and New York Stock Exchange (symbol NTR), with a market capitalization of $34 billion as of January 2018. It was formed through the merger of PotashCorp and Agrium, in a transaction that closed on January 1, 2018.
